presets.name: Sepia
presets.summary: Four warm browns behind the stripes.
presets.description: The shape color follows the background automatically, picking whichever of black and white contrasts more, so changing the palette is enough to carry the whole picture.

presets.name: Greyscale
presets.summary: Four greys, no hue at all.
presets.description: Useful for a print stylesheet, a disabled state, or anywhere color would carry meaning it should not. The shape still flips between black and white for contrast.

presets.name: Duotone
presets.description: A single background hue means every avatar in a set shares it, and only the stripes changes. The most restrained this style gets.

presets.name: Muted
presets.summary: Six dusty backgrounds instead of the bright ones.
presets.description: The style ships a saturated background palette. This trades it for dusty tones, for interfaces where the avatar should be present without being the loudest thing on screen.

presets.name: Electric
presets.description: The other direction on the same lever: six colors past anything the style ships. The shape flips to whichever of black and white survives them.

presets.name: Pastel Wall
presets.description: The lightest way to make a set of avatars feel like it belongs together. The shape goes black against all five.

presets.name: Bold Pop
presets.description: The loud counterpart to Pastel Wall, strong enough that the avatar holds its own against a busy page.

presets.name: Sunrise
presets.summary: A warm gradient behind the stripes.
presets.description: Shows the gradient background options: two colors, a linear fill and a fixed angle. The seed still decides which of the two ends up on top.

presets.name: Stencil
presets.summary: One background for everyone, only the shape varies.
presets.description: Every avatar gets the same near-black ground, so nothing distinguishes them but the drawing itself. That turns a set from a group of portraits into an icon sheet, which is what you want in a toolbar or a legend.
